data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (clearly visible paired leaflets attached at the same node along the rachis in multiple images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped closely along the stems)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (leaves are clearly composed of multiple leaflets attached to a central rachis)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): unclear (the terminal leaflet is not consistently visible to confirm the presence of a terminal leaflet)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 4 (visible on the most distinct leaf structure in the foreground)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): opposite (leaflets are arranged in pairs along the rachis)
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (margins appear smooth, though some minor physical damage is present)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (leaflets are broadly oval-shaped, widest near the middle)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (leaf tips taper to a distinct point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (leaf bases appear broadly rounded)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a central midrib is visible with secondary veins branching off it)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, relatively close and parallel spacing, branching from the midrib
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (leaf surfaces are glossy and reflect light)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (surface appears smooth without visible hairs)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles connecting leaflets to the rachis appear short)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear rounded in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stems appear rigid and lignified)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stems appear smooth)
    19. Stem color: brown to dark brown (visible on thinner stems)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (stems appear relatively smooth without prominent ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are clearly visible at the leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no pulvinus is visible at the leaf base)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent

F. Notes: The plant exhibits pinnately compound leaves with opposite leaflets. Several leaves show signs of physical damage, including holes and missing margins. Some leaf surfaces display irregular yellowish-green mottling or discoloration. The leaves are glossy and wet. A pink tag is visible in the background, indicating the plant is being monitored.
